content.text: {"concept_key":"c5-maths-addition-of-like-fractions","title":"Adding Like Fractions","quick":"When fractions have the same bottom number (denominator), just add the top numbers (numerators). The denominator stays the same because the pieces are the same size.","full":"Think of a roti cut into 8 equal pieces. If Ravi eats 3 pieces (3/8) and Sita eats 2 pieces (2/8), together they ate 5 pieces out of the same 8. Only the numerators (3 and 2) add up to 5, because the size of each piece (denominator 8) doesn't change — it's still cut into 8ths. So 3/8 + 2/8 = 5/8.","traps":["Adding denominators too (writing 5/16 instead of 5/8)","Forgetting to check if the answer fraction can be simplified","Mixing up numerator and denominator when adding"],"misconception":"Child thinks both top and bottom numbers should be added together, like regular whole number addition.","parent_questions":[{"q":"If a roti is cut into 8 pieces and you eat 2 pieces, then eat 1 more, how many pieces total, and how do you write it as a fraction?","expected_answer_hint":"3 pieces out of 8, written as 3/8"},{"q":"Why don't we add the denominators when adding 3/8 and 2/8?","expected_answer_hint":"Because the pizza/roti is still cut into the same 8 equal pieces, so the piece size doesn't change"}],"check_question":{"q":"Rani ate 2/6 of a cake and Mohan ate 3/6 of the same cake. How much did they eat together?","options":["5/6","5/12","6/6"],"correct_index":0,"right_feedback":"Correct! Add only the numerators: 2+3=5, denominator stays 6.","wrong_feedback":"Not quite. Keep the denominator same (6) and just add the numerators: 2+3=5, so 5/6."},"illustration":{"scene_prompt":"A round pizza cut into eight equal slices on a table, with two children sitting nearby about to eat.","labels":[{"text":"Ravi","position":"left"},{"text":"Sita","position":"right"},{"text":"3/8","position":"top-left"},{"text":"2/8","position":"top-right"}]}}
